gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the ALLPOWERS S2000 and S2000 Pro use ternary (NCM) cells rather than LiFePO4. Their kits are the cheapest per Wh under $700, but the S2000 Pro is rated 2,500+ cycles to 80% and the S2000 only '1000+ life cycles', against BLUETTI's 4,000 cycles to 80% for the Elite 100 V2. StorageReview measured just 920 Wh out of the S2000 Pro's rated 1,451 Wh.
standout_why: PowerSized (/solar-generator-kits/, cited in both chats) lists only price, Wh, AC W, panel W and solar cap for its two kits under $700. Its own text gives no cycle life, surge or chemistry. StormWatts (same-panel-watts comparison, cited) covers 24 kits and states no AC watts, surge, cycle life or chemistry; it normalises only panel watts against the solar cap. BLUETTI's /pages/solar-generator/ page returned HTTP 429 and was not read. None of these pages puts cycle life on one end-of-life basis, separates surge from continuous, or flags a non-LFP kit. ChatGPT's own answer says to 'prioritize a LiFePO4 battery', which the S2000 / S2000 Pro kits fail.
decides: Sorted by price per Wh, the ALLPOWERS S2000 Pro + SE100 kit ($673.74 link price, ships now, 1,451 Wh, $0.46/Wh) would be the ship-now pick under $700. The S2000 Pro + SF200 and S2000 + SF200 kits ($612.90, pre-orders for Nov 19 and Nov 20) would be the cheaper wait options. Once chemistry and cycle life are put on one basis, all three drop out for a shopper who follows ChatGPT's own LiFePO4 rule. That leaves the LFP kits: BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 (4,000 cycles to 80%, 3,600 W surge, but a pre-order until mid-December), ALLPOWERS P1800 (LiFePO4, 3,000+ cycles with no end-of-life % stated, pre-order) and the ship-now BLUETTI Elite 100 mini kits. I did not source the Elite 100 mini's chemistry or cycle life, so whoever writes the page must confirm it before naming it the pick. The table also shows that EcoFlow's DELTA 3 Classic solar generator lists at $729 on us.ecoflow.com today, not the $659 ChatGPT showed, and that EcoFlow states cycle life in years, not cycles.
